statement: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at exactly 3 o'clock?

figure.alt: A clock face with the hour hand pointing at 3 and the minute hand pointing at 12, with the angle between them marked.

choices.misconception: I gave the angle for one hour mark instead of the three hour marks between the hands.
I divided the right angle in half, as if a quarter of the clock were 45 degrees.
I used a third of the clock face rather than a quarter of it.
I read 3 o'clock as the hands pointing in opposite directions.

hints: Work out how many degrees one hour mark is worth, then count how many hour marks lie between the two hands at this exact time.
One hour mark is 360 divided by 12 = 30 degrees. At 3 o'clock the hands are 3 marks apart, so the angle is 3 x 30 = 90 degrees.

solutions.reliable: The 12 hour marks divide 360 degrees, so each mark is 30 degrees. At exactly 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3, which is 3 marks apart. The angle is 3 x 30 = 90 degrees. The transferable idea: convert hour marks to degrees once and reuse the 30 for every clock question.
solutions.elegant: Three o'clock is exactly a quarter turn round the face, and a quarter of 360 is 90.

whyOnTest: It fixes the 30-degrees-per-hour-mark fact that every harder clock question is built on.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
